subject: maths
title: Measuring Length, Mass and Capacity
seo_title: Year 3 Measuring Worksheets: Length, Mass and Capacity (Free, with Answer Key)
standard_text: Measure and compare objects using familiar metric units of length, mass and capacity, and instruments with labelled markings
meta_desc: Free Year 3 maths worksheets on measuring: choose metric units and estimate, measure length with a ruler, read scales in g and kg and jugs in mL and L, and compare measures in word problems. 100 questions with an answer key, matched to the Australian Curriculum and useful for NAPLAN.
key_big: Choose a unit that fits, start at 0, and find what one mark is worth.
key_sub: 1 m = 100 cm, 1 kg = 1000 g and 1 L = 1000 mL. Compare measures in the same unit: 1 kg is heavier than 900 g.
body_html:
What we measure

Length is how long something is. Mass is how heavy it is. Capacity is how much a container holds. Each one has its own units and its own tool.

MeasureUnitsTool
Lengthmillimetres (mm), centimetres (cm), metres (m), kilometres (km)ruler, tape measure
Massgrams (g), kilograms (kg)scales
Capacitymillilitres (mL), litres (L)measuring jug, measuring cup

Key facts: 1 m = 100 cm, 1 cm = 10 mm, 1 kg = 1000 g, 1 L = 1000 mL.

Choose a unit and estimate

Small things use small units. Big things use big units. Compare with something you know.

Familiar itemAbout
The width of your little finger1 cm
A classroom door (height)2 m
A paper clip1 g
A bag of sugar1 kg
A teaspoon5 mL
A can of soft drink375 mL
A carton of milk1 L or 2 L

Measure with a ruler

Line up one end of the object with 0, not with 1 and not with the edge of the ruler. Read the number at the other end.

If the object does not start at 0, take away the start from the end, or count the spaces.

Read a scale or a jug

Not every mark has a number. First work out what one mark is worth: the jump between two numbers ÷ the number of spaces. Then count on from the number before.

Compare with the same unit

To compare, change both measures to the same unit first. Never compare just the numbers.

Which is heavier?

1 kg or 900 g?

1 kg = 1000 g. 1000 g is more than 900 g.

Answer: 1 kg is heavier

How much is left?

Ava has a 600 mL water bottle and drinks 250 mL.

Drinking takes water away, so subtract: 600 − 250 = 350.

Answer: 350 mL

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Choosing km for a pencil, or kg for a lengthPick a length unit that fits the size: mm, cm, m or km
Starting at 1 or at the edge of the rulerStart at 0, or take away the start from the end
Counting every mark on a scale as 1 or 10Work out what one mark is worth first
Thinking 900 g is more than 1 kgChange to the same unit: 1 kg = 1000 g
Writing the answer without a unitAlways write the unit: 7 cm, 350 mL, 3 kg

faq.q: What measurement do Year 3 students learn in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: Year 3 students choose suitable metric units, estimate, and measure and compare length (mm, cm, m, km), mass (g, kg) and capacity (mL, L) using rulers, scales and jugs with labelled markings.

faq.q: How do you read a scale when not every mark has a number?
faq.a: Count the spaces between two labelled numbers and divide the jump by the spaces to find what one mark is worth. Then count on from the number before the needle or water line.

faq.q: Is measurement part of the Year 3 NAPLAN numeracy test?
faq.a: Yes. NAPLAN numeracy includes measurement, so Year 3 students may be asked to read rulers, scales and jugs, choose units and compare measures.

faq.q: What are good benchmarks for estimating mass and capacity?
faq.a: A paper clip is about 1 g and a bag of sugar is about 1 kg. A teaspoon holds about 5 mL and a carton of milk holds 1 L or 2 L.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the length of a pencil?
items.e: A pencil is short and fits on a ruler, so use centimetres. Kilometres are for long trips, like a drive to the next town.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the length of the school swimming pool?
items.e: A pool is long, but you can walk along it in a minute, so use metres. Litres measure capacity, not length.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the distance from Sydney to Melbourne?
items.e: Sydney to Melbourne is a long trip by car or plane, so use kilometres.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the mass of a watermelon?
items.e: A watermelon is heavy, so use kilograms. Litres measure how much a container holds.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the mass of a strawberry?
items.e: A strawberry is very light, so use grams.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure how much water a bathtub holds?
items.e: A bathtub holds a lot of water, so use litres.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure how much medicine fits on a spoon?
items.e: A spoon holds only a little, so use millilitres.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the mass of a school backpack?
items.e: A full backpack is quite heavy, so use kilograms.

items.q: Which unit is best to measure the length of a cricket pitch?
items.e: A cricket pitch is about 20 m long. You can walk along it in a short time, so use metres.

items.q: Which unit measures mass?
items.e: Mass is how heavy something is. We measure mass in grams and kilograms. Kilometres sound like kilograms, but they measure length.

items.q: Which unit measures capacity?
items.e: Capacity is how much a container holds. We measure it in millilitres and litres.

items.q: Choose the best estimate. A classroom door is about ☐ tall.
items.e: You are about 1 m 30 cm tall, and a door is a bit taller than an adult. That is about 2 m. 2 cm is shorter than your finger.

items.q: Choose the best estimate. A new pencil is about ☐ long.
items.e: A pencil fits on a 30 cm ruler, so it is about 18 cm long. 18 m is longer than a classroom.

items.q: Choose the best estimate. A Year 3 student is about ☐ tall.
items.e: Most Year 3 students are between 1 m and 1 m 50 cm tall. 130 cm fits. 13 cm is the size of a hand.

items.q: Choose the best estimate. A large carton of milk holds about ☐.
items.e: Big milk cartons from the supermarket hold 2 L. 2 mL is less than half a teaspoon.

items.q: Choose the best estimate. A can of soft drink holds about ☐.
items.e: Australian drink cans hold 375 mL. 375 L would fill about two bathtubs.

items.q: Choose the best estimate. A whole watermelon has a mass of about ☐.
items.e: A whole watermelon is heavy to carry, about 6 kg. 6 g is as light as six paper clips, and 60 kg is as heavy as a grown-up.

items.q: Choose the best estimate. A paper clip has a mass of about ☐.
items.e: A paper clip is very light. 1 g is about the mass of one paper clip.

items.q: Choose the best estimate. A teaspoon holds about ☐.
items.e: A teaspoon holds only a little, about 5 mL. 5 L would half fill a bucket.

items.q: Choose the best estimate. A bag of sugar from the supermarket has a mass of about ☐.
items.e: Sugar is often sold in 1 kg bags. 100 kg is heavier than a grown-up.

items.q: How many centimetres are in 1 metre?
items.e: A metre ruler has 100 centimetres marked on it. So 1 m = 100 cm.

items.q: How many millimetres are in 1 centimetre?
items.e: Look at a ruler. There are 10 small spaces in each centimetre. So 1 cm = 10 mm.
The pencil starts at 0 and ends at 7. So it is 7 cm long. Count the spaces, not the marks.
The crayon starts at 0 and ends at 5. So it is 5 cm long. Count the spaces, not the marks.
The eraser starts at 0 and ends at 4. So it is 4 cm long. Count the spaces, not the marks.
The piece of ribbon starts at 0 and ends at 8. So it is 8 cm long. Count the spaces, not the marks.
The crayon starts at 0 and ends at 6. So it is 6 cm long. Count the spaces, not the marks.
The pencil starts at 2, not at 0. It ends at 9. 9 − 2 = 7, so it is 7 cm long. You can also count the spaces: there are 7.
The crayon starts at 1, not at 0. It ends at 6. 6 − 1 = 5, so it is 5 cm long. You can also count the spaces: there are 5.
The eraser starts at 3, not at 0. It ends at 7. 7 − 3 = 4, so it is 4 cm long. You can also count the spaces: there are 4.
The piece of ribbon starts at 2, not at 0. It ends at 8. 8 − 2 = 6, so it is 6 cm long. You can also count the spaces: there are 6.
The pencil starts at 1, not at 0. It ends at 9. 9 − 1 = 8, so it is 8 cm long. You can also count the spaces: there are 8.
The crayon starts at 4, not at 0. It ends at 9. 9 − 4 = 5, so it is 5 cm long. You can also count the spaces: there are 5.

items.q: Lachlan puts the end of his pencil at 1 on the ruler, not at 0. The other end is at 8. How long is it?
items.e: He started at 1, so the number at the end is 1 too big. 8 − 1 = 7 cm.

items.q: Harper puts the end of her book at 1 on the ruler, not at 0. The other end is at 12. How long is it?
items.e: She started at 1, so the number at the end is 1 too big. 12 − 1 = 11 cm.
The crayon goes past 4 cm and then 6 small marks more. 4 cm = 40 mm, and 40 + 6 = 46. So it is 46 mm long.
The pencil goes past 6 cm and then 3 small marks more. 6 cm = 60 mm, and 60 + 3 = 63. So it is 63 mm long.
The eraser goes past 3 cm and then 5 small marks more. 3 cm = 30 mm, and 30 + 5 = 35. So it is 35 mm long.
The pencil starts at 2 cm, not at 0. It ends at 7 cm and 4 small marks, which is 74 mm. 2 cm = 20 mm. 74 − 20 = 54 mm.

items.q: Which tool is best to measure the length of your desk?
items.e: Length is measured with a ruler or a tape measure. A jug measures capacity, scales measure mass and a clock measures time.

sets.title: Read scales: mass in g and kg

items.q: How many grams are in 1 kilogram?
items.e: Kilo means 1000. So 1 kg = 1000 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a block of cheese. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 200 ÷ 2 = 100 g. The needle is 1 mark past 200: 200 + 100 = 300 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bunch of bananas. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 200 ÷ 2 = 100 g. The needle is 1 mark past 600: 600 + 100 = 700 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of apples. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 200 ÷ 2 = 100 g. The needle is 1 mark past 800: 800 + 100 = 900 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a tub of yoghurt. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 200 ÷ 2 = 100 g. The needle is 1 mark past 400: 400 + 100 = 500 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a loaf of bread. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 g. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 500 ÷ 5 = 100 g. The needle is 3 marks past 500: 500 + 300 = 800 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a box of cereal. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 g. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 500 ÷ 5 = 100 g. The needle is 4 marks past 0: 400 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of mandarins. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 g. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 500 ÷ 5 = 100 g. The needle is 4 marks past 500: 500 + 400 = 900 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of carrots. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 g. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 500 ÷ 5 = 100 g. The needle is 3 marks past 0: 300 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of an avocado and a mango. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 g. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 100 ÷ 2 = 50 g. The needle is 1 mark past 300: 300 + 50 = 350 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of an orange. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 g. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 100 ÷ 2 = 50 g. The needle is 1 mark past 100: 100 + 50 = 150 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of dog food. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 2 kg. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 1 kg. The needle is 1 mark past 6: 6 + 1 = 7 kg.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a pile of library books. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 2 kg. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 1 kg. The needle is 1 mark past 2: 2 + 1 = 3 kg.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a pumpkin. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 2 kg. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 1 kg. The needle is 1 mark past 4: 4 + 1 = 5 kg.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a suitcase. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 5 kg. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 1 kg. The needle is 2 marks past 10: 10 + 2 = 12 kg.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of potting mix. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 5 kg. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 1 kg. The needle is 2 marks past 15: 15 + 2 = 17 kg.

items.q: The scale shows a bag of flour. How much more flour is needed to make 1 kg?
items.e: The needle is at 600 g. 1 kg = 1000 g. 1000 − 600 = 400 g more.

items.q: The scale shows a bowl of cherries. The empty bowl has a mass of 100 g. What is the mass of the cherries?
items.e: Each mark is 50 g, so the needle is at 450 g. Take away the bowl: 450 − 100 = 350 g.

items.q: Which bag of fruit is heavier, and by how much?
items.e: Each mark is 100 g. A shows 600 g and B shows 900 g. B is heavier. 900 − 600 = 300 g.

items.q: Which bag of fruit is heavier, and by how much?
items.e: Each mark is 100 g. A shows 800 g and B shows 300 g. A is heavier. 800 − 300 = 500 g.

sets.title: Read jugs: capacity in mL and L

items.q: How many millilitres are in 1 litre?
items.e: Milli means one thousandth. So 1 L = 1000 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 mL. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each line is 200 ÷ 2 = 100 mL. The water is 1 line above 200: 200 + 100 = 300 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 mL. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each line is 200 ÷ 2 = 100 mL. The water is 1 line above 600: 600 + 100 = 700 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 mL. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each line is 200 ÷ 2 = 100 mL. The water is 1 line above 800: 800 + 100 = 900 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 mL. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each line is 500 ÷ 2 = 250 mL. The water is 1 line up from the bottom: 250 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 mL. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each line is 500 ÷ 2 = 250 mL. The water is 1 line above 500: 500 + 250 = 750 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The jug goes from 0 at the bottom to 1000 mL. There are 4 spaces, so each line is 1000 ÷ 4 = 250 mL. The water is 2 lines up from the bottom: 500 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 mL. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each line is 250 ÷ 5 = 50 mL. The water is 3 lines above 250: 250 + 150 = 400 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 mL. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each line is 250 ÷ 5 = 50 mL. The water is 3 lines above 500: 500 + 150 = 650 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 mL. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each line is 250 ÷ 5 = 50 mL. The water is 1 line above 500: 500 + 50 = 550 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 mL. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each line is 250 ÷ 5 = 50 mL. The water is 2 lines above 750: 750 + 100 = 850 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 mL. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each line is 100 ÷ 2 = 50 mL. The water is 1 line above 200: 200 + 50 = 250 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 mL. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each line is 100 ÷ 2 = 50 mL. The water is 1 line above 300: 300 + 50 = 350 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 mL. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each line is 500 ÷ 5 = 100 mL. The water is 3 lines above 1000: 1000 + 300 = 1300 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 mL. There are 5 spaces between numbers, so each line is 500 ÷ 5 = 100 mL. The water is 2 lines above 1500: 1500 + 200 = 1700 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 mL. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each line is 500 ÷ 2 = 250 mL. The water is 1 line above 1000: 1000 + 250 = 1250 mL.

items.q: How much more water is needed to fill the jug to 1 L?
items.e: Each line is 100 mL, so the water is at 400 mL. 1 L = 1000 mL. 1000 − 400 = 600 mL more.

items.q: Noah pours 250 mL of water out of the jug. How much is left?
items.e: The water is at 800 mL. Water is poured out, so subtract: 800 − 250 = 550 mL.

items.q: How many 250 mL cups of water fill a 1 L jug?
items.e: 1 L = 1000 mL. Count by 250: 250, 500, 750, 1000. That is 4 cups.

items.q: Which tool is best to measure 200 mL of milk for a recipe?
items.e: Capacity is measured with a measuring jug or a measuring cup. Scales measure mass.

sets.title: Compare measures and solve word problems

items.q: Which is the heaviest?
items.e: Change them all to grams: 1 kg = 1000 g. 1000 g is more than 990 g and 900 g. Do not just compare the numbers 1 and 990.

items.q: Which is the longest?
items.e: Change them all to centimetres: 2 m = 200 cm. 200 cm is more than 190 cm. Do not just compare the numbers 2 and 190.

items.q: Which holds the most?
items.e: Change them all to millilitres: 1 L = 1000 mL. 1000 mL is more than 950 mL. Do not just compare the numbers 1 and 950.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 1 kg = 1000 g. 1000 g is more than 900 g. Do not compare only the numbers 1 and 900.

items.q: Which list goes from the shortest to the longest?
items.e: Change them to centimetres: 1 m = 100 cm. 80 < 100 < 120.

items.q: Amelia has a 600 mL water bottle. She drinks 250 mL at recess. How much water is left?
items.e: Drinking takes water away, so subtract: 600 − 250 = 350 mL.

items.q: At the market, Sienna's watermelon has a mass of 6 kg. A rockmelon has a mass of 2 kg. How much heavier is the watermelon?
items.e: How much heavier means find the difference: 6 − 2 = 4 kg.

items.q: Noah's lunchbox has a mass of 400 g. His drink bottle has a mass of 600 g. What is their total mass?
items.e: Add: 400 + 600 = 1000 g. 1000 g = 1 kg. It is not 10 g: 4 hundreds + 6 hundreds = 10 hundreds.

items.q: Ethan's backpack has a mass of 5 kg. He takes out 2 kg of library books. What is the mass of the backpack now?
items.e: Taking out means subtract: 5 − 2 = 3 kg.

items.q: The school canteen has 8 kg of sausages for the sausage sizzle. They cook 5 kg. How many kilograms are left?
items.e: Subtract what was cooked: 8 − 5 = 3 kg.

items.q: Isla has 85 cm of ribbon. She cuts off 30 cm for a card. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: Cutting off means subtract: 85 − 30 = 55 cm.

items.q: A sunflower in the school garden was 35 cm tall. It grew 18 cm more. How tall is it now?
items.e: Add: 35 + 18. 5 + 8 = 13, so regroup 10 ones as 1 ten. 35 + 18 = 53 cm.

items.q: At the athletics carnival, Mei jumps 185 cm. Ruby jumps 210 cm. How much further does Ruby jump?
William is 128 cm tall. His dad is 180 cm tall. How much taller is his dad?
items.e: Find the difference: 180 − 128 = 52 cm. Check: 128 + 52 = 180.

items.q: Oliver rides his bike 3 km to the beach and 3 km back home. How far does he ride altogether?
items.e: There and back is 3 km + 3 km = 6 km.

items.q: A jug holds 1 L of cordial. Four cups of 200 mL are poured for a picnic. How much cordial is left in the jug?
Matilda has a 1 kg bag of flour. She uses 350 g to bake Anzac biscuits. How much flour is left?
Aarav has a 2 L bottle of orange juice. He pours 500 mL into glasses for the family. How much juice is left in the bottle?
items.e: 2 L = 2000 mL. Subtract: 2000 − 500 = 1500 mL. Do not take 2 from 500: change to the same unit first.

items.q: A paddling pool holds 60 L of water. A bucket holds 10 L. How many full buckets fill the pool?
items.e: Count by 10 L: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. That is 6 buckets. 60 ÷ 10 = 6.

items.q: A brown worm is 45 mm long. A pink worm is 6 cm long. Which worm is longer, and by how much?
items.e: 6 cm = 60 mm. 60 mm is more than 45 mm, so the pink worm is longer. 60 − 45 = 15 mm. Do not take 6 from 45: change to the same unit first.
